ratings_why.fun: Keep-or-swap is a real mid-game choice and Hollin and Bettie give a late climb, but the first turns are small bodies whose value depends on what the shop rolls.
ratings_why.distinct: 8 over 7 because Exchange makes the shop a second board you trade with, and stealing the enemy's text off the visible next board is a new reason to place units; no current tribe touches the shop or the enemy's text.

verdict_why: The Fetch's rules clash with One of each and Tam's text is unreadable when worn; both are small wording fixes.

points.text: The Fetch's Stock is a Changeling, so taking the biggest unit's Guise strips that Guise from the carry under One of each; and a non-Changeling carry has no Guise to copy. Say the Stock copies the biggest unit's text and Guise and ignores One of each.
Tam Twice's text says it wears two Guises, so a Changeling wearing Tam's Guise has a Guise that asks for two more Guises. Say whether that works or that Tam's text can't be worn.
The early climb rests on Cradle Kit finding a good text in the shop. A fallback when the shop is poor, such as keeping a Guise from a unit you refresh away, would steady turns 1 to 3.
Pip Unlike's mirror only matters for texts that name a side, which is rare. Pip could also flip which enemy or slot a text picks, so it has a use in most lobbies.
Bettie Underhill rewards Exchanges from turn 2 onward; show the game's Exchange count on the board so players plan for her before they see her.

standouts.why: Penny Second uses the visible next board: place her across their key unit, steal its Start of Combat and silence it.
Long-Stay Hollin is a clear direction card that turns keeping high-tier Guises into big steady growth.
Coat-Peg Steward now moves buffs onto the shop's best unit, a fresh way to upgrade a board without losing its stats.

weakest.why: Pip Unlike's mirror does nothing for most texts, so it is a worse Cradle Kit at Tier 2.
Counter Stand-In needs you to sell the unit whose text you wanted, a narrow trigger for a Tier 3 enabler.
Weeks-Old Hob's +1/+1 a turn is a slow seed with a 1/3 body that doesn't win early fights.

flags.note: Bettie Underhill's pay grows with every Exchange in the game, and Midnight Swap plus the Officer make Exchanges cheap, so late turns can hand each Changeling +15/+15 or more.
Placement Officer with Wicker Moll: Exchange away a Stock, take a shop unit free and Moll leaves a new Stock, so a free unit every turn (two with goldens).
Keeper of the Lost Hour with the Lady Under the Hill doubles every stolen and borrowed fight trigger on one body; the high roll worth the owner's eye.
The Fetch's Stock taking the carry's Guise conflicts with One of each, and a non-Changeling carry has no Guise.
Tam Twice's text worn as a Guise asks for two more Guises; the rules don't say what happens.
